title: PreFix: Optimizing the Performance of Heap-Intensive Applications
problem: Heap-intensive applications suffer from poor spatial locality despite known concentration of accesses in a small fraction of objects. Prior techniques (HDS, HALO) achieve imperfect separation and cannot reorder objects across allocations.
motivation: A small fraction of heap objects account for majority of accesses and cache misses; improving spatial locality through better object placement can significantly improve performance.
method: PreFix watches your program as it runs and uses context information to identify which data objects get accessed most frequently (hot objects) with high accuracy. It then reserves specific memory regions ahead of time and places these frequently-used objects there, allowing it to group them together even if they were originally allocated separately. The system also recycles this reserved memory—when one object is no longer needed, it reuses that space for a new object, saving memory when object lifetimes don't overlap.
key_novelty: PreFix's core idea is using runtime context information to identify hot objects with near-perfect precision, enabling it to reorder and group frequently-accessed data together in memory.
contributions: Context-based mechanism for high-precision hot object identification
Near-perfect separation of hot objects in dedicated memory regions
Object recycling optimization for reuse of preallocated memory
21.7% average execution time reduction (vs. 7.3% for HDS, 14% for HALO)
limitations: Limited memory footprint analysis; scalability to very large heap sizes and multi-threaded scenarios not discussed.
primary_theme: Precision hot object isolation for cache locality
